title: Affine Frobenius-kernel coordinate ideals and distribution pushforward
statement: Let $F$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $G,H$ affine $F$-group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Use their canonical coordinate Hopf algebras and convolution duals [def-sfb-affine-group-distribution-calculus] and the actual coordinate restriction $i^*:F[G]\to F[H]$ of a homomorphism $i:H\to G$ [def-sfb-rational-highest-weight-data]. For $q\in\mathbf N$ define $J_q(G)=(c^q\mid c\in F[G],\ \epsilon(c)=0)$. Say $i$ presents the $q$th Frobenius kernel if it is a closed subgroup inclusion and $\ker i^*=J_q(G)$. In characteristic $p>0$ with $q=p^r$, this is precisely the affine kernel of the relative Frobenius with coordinate map $c\otimes a\mapsto ac^q$: pulling back the identity gives this ideal. The closed inclusion and its ideal determine the kernel up to its unique isomorphism over $G$. For any $i$ define distribution pushforward $i_*a=a\circ i^*$ on the full convolution duals. No kernel representative or unrelated map is chosen.

from.place: The finite-kernel adjacent-Borel calculation: canonical Frobenius kernels and their distribution inclusions, before applying a module action. det-thm-sf-ctf-stability-direct-images, proof (3), alteration reduction through ILO X Lemma 2.2: dimension induction in the marked plurinodal input; one relative curve, de Jong Theorem 2.4, Lemmas 5.5 and 5.7, before induction on its base; replacement prerequisite: de Jong Lemma 3.7, printed p.608, including the prime-to-characteristic level-structure choice which makes the base alteration generically etale; §3.6 supplies the smooth genus-at-least-two input. This is stable pointed-curve extension, not stable modification of a specified target pair. Moduli prerequisite: projective compactification with prime-to-characteristic level structure and its universal stable family, used before taking the closure of a generic lift. Projectivity of the unpointed stable coarse moduli scheme. Supporting input: Projective geometric quotients of closed stable loci for PGL. Affine-chart proof of the projective PGL quotient: Power lifting and finite generation for PGL invariants. Supporting argument: Haboush symmetric-power lifting for a trivial quotient representation. Supporting representation-theoretic input: Steinberg endomorphisms detect a nonzero fixed vector. Supporting Self-duality of rho section modules at characteristic-dependent weights. Supporting input: Positive-characteristic simplicity step, using irreducibility of the Steinberg induced module rather than assuming self-duality. Numerical input to the dimension comparison: Weyl dimension of the induced module. Supporting Kempf vanishing for dominant flag line bundles. Positive-characteristic Andersen–Haboush argument: trivial pushforward of M_((p^r-1)rho), before the Serre twisting calculation. Supporting input: Lemma 2.3, second assertion, and Lemma 2.1, printed pp.153--155: H^0(u,V(lambda))=K v_lambda for p-restricted dominant lambda. With roots positive in Lie(B), V(lambda)=Gamma(M_{-w0 lambda}). Supporting input: Simple-root distributions and infinitesimal subalgebra calculus. Supporting input: pinning-compatible integral-to-geometric distribution comparison, with all positive root divided powers, before simple-root generation. Integral-root-model prerequisite before the comparison: integral Chevalley construction and a positive-root coordinate chart; integral matrix-closure construction: the big cell and its Weyl translates, before identifying the special fibre. Supporting input: Integral closure atlas, exhaustion of each special fibre: exclude extra components using the generic and special identity-component big-cell dimensions. Supporting input: Lemma 3.7 (first assertion, the Iwahori--Matsumoto maximal-boundedness statement) and its application in Proposition 4.3, second paragraph, printed pp.7-8; Cartan double-coset input used to prove the maximal-boundedness prerequisite, before the torus-powers argument. Supporting input: Theorem 1.3, implication (1) to (3), printed pp.1, 6; Definition 3.4 and Lemma 3.6, printed pp.5-6. The complete-DVR cocharacter form, before the non-complete descent of Theorem 4.1. Supporting input: Section 2, Claim 2, printed p.2; Section 3, proof of Theorem 1.3, (1) implies (2), printed p.6, removes the residue-field and splitness restrictions. Supporting input: Claim 2: choose a linear embedding and use reductivity to make the homogeneous quotient affine. Supporting input: Alper, Adequate moduli spaces and geometrically reductive group schemes, Theorem 9.7.5, Proposition 9.3.1(i), Lemma 9.2.5(2),(3), printed pp.522,524,527--528. WANTED local copy; read https://content.algebraicgeometry.nl/2014-4/2014-4-022.pdf.
